topicName: The Fall of the Roman Republic

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Fall of the Roman Republic
cards.back: The Gracchi brothers (Tiberius d.133 BC, Gaius d.121 BC) tried to reform land distribution; both were killed by senatorial opposition

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Fall of the Roman Republic
cards.back: Marius reformed the army: soldiers swore loyalty to their general (not the state), giving ambitious commanders private armies

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Fall of the Roman Republic
cards.back: Sulla marched his army on Rome (88 BC) — the first time a Roman general used military force against the city itself

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Fall of the Roman Republic
cards.back: The First Triumvirate (60 BC): Caesar, Pompey and Crassus dominated politics; it was an unofficial power-sharing agreement

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Fall of the Roman Republic
cards.back: Caesar crossed the Rubicon (49 BC), starting civil war; he defeated Pompey and became dictator for life

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Fall of the Roman Republic
cards.back: Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March (15 March 44 BC) by senators who feared he wanted to be king

cards.front: What should you know about gcse ancient history exam tips — the fall of the roman republic?
cards.back: 1. For The Fall of the Roman Republic, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with The Fall of the Roman Republic 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
Explain why the Roman Republic collapsed and describe the roles of the Gracchi, Marius and Caesar in its downfall. [6 marks]
